dbe_source.recommendation: sin(A + B) expands to sin A cos B + cos A sin B. cos(A + B) expands to cos A cos B - sin A sin B. The first product in sin(A+B) has sin, in cos(A+B) has cos.

lesson.concept: sin(A + B) expands to sin A cos B + cos A sin B. cos(A + B) expands to cos A cos B - sin A sin B. The first product in sin(A+B) has sin, in cos(A+B) has cos.
lesson.why: This is one of the most frequent errors DBE reported for this section.

work: First product: sin A cos B.
Second product: cos A sin B.
So sin(A + B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B.

probe.expected: cos A cos B - sin A sin B

learner_message: You used the cosine expansion where the sine expansion was needed. sin(A + B) starts with sin A cos B; cos(A + B) starts with cos A cos B.
